Birds of a Feather, a 3D pigeon flight and crowd-combat game

The world used to be kind to pigeons: war heroes, peace bringers, companions. Now they are pests. Fly across the city as the chosen pigeon, win over scattered birds, and grow a flock big enough to take on the enemy leaders keeping pigeonkind down. Part 3D exploration, part crowd combat, where your followers are your health bar, your army and your responsibility all at once.

Everything in the build is mine: concept, systems, flocking follower AI, enemy leaders, level layout, UI, dialogue and the build itself, all scoped and shipped inside jam deadlines. It is the clearest proof of range I have:
I can design a game and then actually make it exist
Followers as a resource: recruiting birds is progression, combat power and risk, all in one number.
Flight as a verb: traversal is the reward loop, so the city is designed around perch-to-perch hops with landmark navigation.
Honest jank: the itch page documents known bugs openly. Shipping and transparency beat polish theatre in a jam build.

★ Winner, Mechanics category, Spain Game Devs Jam II

Blaster Buds is a duel of wits on a grid, set in the vacuum of space. You and your mirrored opponent share every input: move and it moves, shoot and it shoots. Victory never comes from outgunning the other side; it comes from reading the level and making the environment fight for you.

The mirror mechanic means every level is designed twice at once: each tile placed for the player is also a tile placed for the opponent. Asymmetric level geometry becomes the only source of advantage, which turns
level design into the game's real antagonist
. That is exactly why the jam awarded it Best Mechanics.
The mirrored-action core mechanic and its rule set (movement, shooting, hazards).
Puzzle levels ordered as a difficulty curve that teaches through play, not tutorials.
A hazard vocabulary (asteroids, walls and pits) that converts symmetry into strategy.

You are the blue bud. Your rival copies every move you make: up and down exactly, left and right mirrored. Rocks stop one of you and not the other. Steer your rival into a black hole without falling into one yourself.

Love at First Bite is a dating sim built around narrative and investigation. You live the life of a vampire surviving through a dating app: swipe right on tasty humans, swipe left when a profile feels off, because some vampires are better at hiding than others. Matches are limited each day, and your thirst only grows while you decide on tonight's dinner.
The game started as our entry to the Indie Spain Jam 2023. The concept held up, so we took it through the PowerUp+ pre-incubation program and founded
to build the full version, now heading to Steam.
· profiles are puzzles. Reading bios, photos and chat behaviour to unmask hidden vampires turns a swipe into a risk/reward decision.
· limited daily matches and a growing thirst meter create a soft timer that forces commitment without hard fail states.
· conversations run on a tension bar: keep the date charmed, don't let suspicion peak.

R4D10HEAD, an inverted-stealth game where moving makes you deafeningly loud and standing still makes you blind. Game and level design by Aitor Morales.
Stealth, except you are the loudest thing in the room.
R4D10HEAD key art — an inverted-stealth game
Stealth, except you are the loudest thing in the room. Move and the whole floor hears you; stand still and you go blind. Every route is a bet.

R4D10HEAD is a stealth game with prop-hunt style interactions. Our little robot cannot help being a nuisance: movement is all or nothing, full speed at full volume, and standing still means going blind while it recharges. Slip past the CORPORATION's guards and cameras, and find the way out.

Classic stealth hands you tools to be quiet. R4D10HEAD takes them away. The core loop trades information for mobility: while you move you are deafeningly loud but you can see; while you stop you are safe but blind. That single inversion drives every other decision. Guards react to noise you cannot avoid making, so the skill is
when to be loud, not how to stay silent
Guard and camera placement built around readable patrol rhythms a player can learn while blind.
Prop-interaction spots that reward planning a route before committing to the noise.
Escalating spaces: teaching rooms first, then layered patrols where routes have to be chained.
Loud when you move, blind when you stop

Viktor's Mayhem, released in Spanish as

, is a TV game show nobody should want to be on. A slot machine rolls your fate, and whatever misfortune it lands on, you carry into an arena fight. Move, dodge and attack your way through it while a delighted host commentates your suffering.

. Random handicaps re-texture the same arena every run, so each curse changes how you have to play rather than simply making the numbers worse. The real work was balancing the misfortunes to stay genuinely fun: cruel enough to earn the show's premise, never so cruel that a run feels lost before it starts.
The show-format game loop: slot machine, then curse, then arena, then payoff.
The misfortune roster and the balance rules that keep it playable.
Combat and arena encounters tuned around WASD movement, dodges and melee attacks.
